questions.stem: A new TCP service fails only during a SYN burst. Which meter should be checked first?
options: Destination tcp_syn_flood packets-per-second meter
Source-keyed tcp_port_scan packets-per-second meter
Concurrent tcp_src_session connection count
Established-session firewall-policy hit counter
feedback: tcp_syn_flood measures SYN arrivals including retransmissions to one destination.
tcp_port_scan keys SYN rate by source and tests scanning behavior.
tcp_src_session counts concurrent connections, not a SYN packet burst.
Forward-policy counters may miss traffic discarded by the earlier DoS check.

questions.stem: A DoS sensor is set to rate 0 with broadcast-like traffic unaffected elsewhere. What does zero mean for enabled anomalies?
options: Drop all traffic matching the enabled anomaly type
Disable all anomaly checks on the ingress interface
Use the model's recommended threshold automatically
Inherit the security policy's session-rate limit
feedback: Fortinet documents zero as a drop-all threshold for the enabled categories.
Disabling requires sensor status changes, not rate zero.
Recommended thresholds are explicit values, not the meaning of zero.
DoS meters do not inherit forwarding-policy session limits.

questions.stem: IKE UDP/500 is dropped before the tunnel daemon sees it. Which evidence most directly tests an early DoS decision?
options: Anomaly log with udp_flood and gateway destination
Firewall-policy accept log for an unrelated TCP flow
IPsec phase-two selector match and proxy ID
Client browser TLS certificate validation trace
feedback: A udp_flood anomaly event with matching peer IP proves pre-policy suppression.
Unrelated TCP success cannot exclude UDP-specific anomaly blocking.
Phase-two selectors do not explain packet loss before IKE processing.
Browser TLS diagnostics are unrelated to IKE UDP admission.

questions.stem: An operator changes continuous to periodical anomaly mode. What changes?
options: Permit the configured packet quota each new period
All packets bypass the configured anomaly threshold
Concurrent-session limits become SYN-only rate meters
Traffic begins matching only explicit proxy policies
feedback: Periodical mode permits the threshold quantity in successive periods.
Anomaly evaluation remains enabled and still drops excess traffic.
The mode does not convert sensor types or their accounting keys.
DoS ingress checks are independent of explicit proxy matching.

questions.stem: A deployed VM suddenly displays the first-run wizard after 252 VDOMs are counted against 250 licenses. Best diagnosis?
options: Management device/VDOM entitlement capacity exceeded
FortiGate forwarding policies were automatically deleted
ADOM workspace locks have expired unexpectedly
FortiAnalyzer archive retention reached its quota
feedback: The counted units exceed entitlement and match the documented wizard symptom.
A management GUI wizard does not imply data-plane policy deletion.
Workspace locks control concurrent edits, not VM entitlement consumption.
FortiAnalyzer log storage quotas do not cause this FortiManager symptom.

questions.stem: Which command best corroborates the licensed versus managed device/VDOM count?
options: diagnose dvm device list plus diagnose debug vminfo
diagnose debug application ike -1 plus route lookup
execute log filter plus diagnose log test
get router info bgp summary plus ping
feedback: The DVM inventory and VM license diagnostics expose counted devices and maximum capacity.
IKE and route checks concern tunnel or forwarding behavior.
Log filters do not enumerate licensed management objects.
BGP neighbors do not determine FortiManager VM license usage.

questions.stem: A new VDOM is added to a managed FortiGate without adding hardware. What should capacity planning consider?
options: VDOM inventory may increase management license consumption
Only the physical chassis can consume management licenses
New VDOMs consume only FortiAnalyzer archive disk
VDOM additions automatically extend FortiManager entitlement
feedback: The management widget counts devices/VDOMs under the applicable license rules.
Chassis count alone can understate VDOM-enabled management consumption.
Log retention is separate from management device/VDOM licensing.
Adding configuration objects does not automatically buy capacity.

questions.stem: A valid FortiManager VM license file is uploaded. Which subsequent behavior is documented?
options: The system restarts to verify the uploaded license
Every managed FortiGate immediately reloads its firewall policy
All ADOMs are merged into the root ADOM
Device inventory is discarded before the next login
feedback: License-file activation includes a FortiManager restart for verification.
VM licensing is not a bulk policy-install transaction.
License verification does not merge ADOM boundaries.
The procedure is not a device-database factory reset.

questions.stem: A basic handler is saved but now needs FOLLOWED_BY semantics. What change is required?
options: Create a correlation handler with the intended sequence
Add a notification profile to the existing basic handler
Increase the report dataset's retention interval
Enable archive-only processing on the existing handler
feedback: Event Handler Type cannot be changed after saving; recreate as correlation.
Notifications are downstream actions and cannot change rule logic.
Report retention does not create temporal correlation operators.
Event handlers evaluate Analytics logs, not Archive-only records.

questions.stem: Two events are seven minutes apart; FOLLOWED_BY threshold duration is five. Expected result?
options: The events fall outside the five-minute time window
The pair matches because source IPs are identical
The second event automatically extends the first window
A notification profile overrides the duration setting
feedback: Correlation requires the sequence to fit within Threshold Duration.
Matching identities do not waive the configured time boundary.
A late event does not retroactively extend the window.
Notification delivery is separate from correlation eligibility.

questions.stem: A handler finds many false positives behind a shared NAT. Which design is strongest?
options: Join on a consistent user identity rather than NAT IP
Join all records solely on the translated source IP
Disable the data selector for all managed devices
Use only the destination TCP port as subject
feedback: A stable user identity reduces accidental joins among NAT-shared clients.
A NAT address can represent many unrelated actors.
Removing scoping increases unrelated events and noise.
Destination ports are rarely unique subjects for user sequences.

questions.stem: An Archive search shows both records but the correlation handler never fires. First pipeline question?
options: Are the records present in Analytics logs for this ADOM?
Was the report exported as a PDF document?
Does the FortiGate have a valid static default route?
Is the dashboard widget using the correct color palette?
feedback: Event handlers consume Analytics logs in the appropriate ADOM.
PDF export is not a prerequisite for event-handler evaluation.
FortiGate routing may matter to ingestion but does not prove Analytics availability.
Widget appearance has no role in correlation input.

questions.stem: An access port uses storm-control rate 0 for broadcast. What is the likely DHCP effect?
options: DHCP Discover broadcasts are suppressed at ingress
DHCP relay always chooses the backup gateway
DHCP offers are converted to unknown unicast
The switch automatically disables STP on that port
feedback: Zero drops all enabled broadcast-category frames, including Discover.
Relay selection is unrelated to a local storm-control threshold.
Storm control does not rewrite DHCP packet classification.
Storm control and STP are separate control mechanisms.

questions.stem: A port override is configured, but the engineer edits only global storm settings. Why no change?
options: Port-level override wins over the global rate setting
The port is using a global routing VRF instead
Storm control requires every port to be a trunk
The switch ignores all traffic after learning MACs
feedback: Port storm-control-mode override supersedes global behavior.
VRFs do not explain port-level storm policy precedence.
Access ports can use storm control; trunking is not required.
Known MAC learning does not disable broadcast and unknown meters.

questions.stem: Which traffic class is distinct from the unknown-unicast storm meter?
options: Unicast frames with a known forwarding-table destination
Unknown unicast frames with no learned destination
Broadcast frames to the Ethernet all-ones address
Unknown multicast frames without group-specific forwarding
feedback: Known unicast is outside the specified unknown-unicast category.
Unknown unicast is precisely what that meter is designed to count.
Broadcast has its own independently enabled sensor.
Unknown multicast has its own separately configured sensor.

questions.stem: A 1000-pps limit works on one switch model but not another under microbursts. What else matters?
options: Burst-size level and model-specific ASIC limits
FortiAnalyzer report-dataset cache expiration time
FortiGate user-group membership refresh interval
FortiManager policy-package revision numbering
feedback: Burst tolerance depends on model and burst-size-level behavior.
Report caching does not change physical switch storm-control bursts.
User groups are unrelated to L2 traffic-class meters.
Policy revisions do not define ASIC burst bucket size.

questions.stem: A FortiAP discovers its controller but loops between SULKING and DTLS_SETUP. Most relevant next check?
options: AP CA trust store and compatible firmware version
SSID airtime fairness and channel-width selection
Client DHCP lease and default gateway renewal
Captive portal RADIUS group assignment precedence
feedback: The documented 231K issue involves missing CA1 trust during DTLS setup.
RF settings matter after AP management joins, not this handshake.
Client DHCP cannot explain the AP control-channel trust failure.
Portal authorization is downstream of AP controller admission.

questions.stem: What does a CAPWAP discovery response prove about AP admission?
options: The controller is reachable, not that DTLS joined
The AP's certificate chain has been fully accepted
All SSIDs are broadcasting with valid encryption
The controller has authorized every discovered serial
feedback: Discovery proves initial reachability but not later join stages.
DTLS certificate validation occurs after discovery.
Client SSID service requires successful AP joining and profile application.
Discovery normally precedes manual or configured automatic authorization.

questions.stem: Which setting allows a controller to create entries for newly discovered APs?
options: Enable ap-discover on the FortiGate management interface
set storm-control-mode override on the switch port
set dtls-policy clear-text on the client SSID
set auto-firmware-upgrade disable on FortiGuard
feedback: ap-discover controls controller acceptance of discovery messages.
Storm control concerns switch frame rates, not AP table creation.
Data-channel DTLS policy does not enable controller discovery.
Firmware auto-upgrade does not determine AP discovery registration.

questions.stem: A 231K lacks Fortinet_CA1.cer on affected firmware. Supported remediation?
options: Install supported fix firmware or newer GA release
Disable all controller certificate checks permanently
Enable blanket AP auto-authorization for every serial
Change the client SSID to open authentication
feedback: Fortinet documents a TAC fix image or supported later firmware.
Bypassing certificate trust is not the documented safe fix.
Authorization cannot supply a missing AP trust anchor.
SSID security does not repair CAPWAP control DTLS.

questions.stem: A switch L2 poll succeeds but no IP address appears for a host. What data source is missing?
options: L3 ARP polling to join IP and MAC identities
Another copy of the same switch MAC table
FortiAnalyzer report dataset for the switch
FortiAP radio profile with a longer beacon interval
feedback: L2 provides MAC and port; L3 ARP supplies IP-to-MAC mapping.
Repeating L2 does not add routed neighbor information.
Reporting data is not the FortiNAC host IP source.
Wireless beacon timing does not populate wired ARP identity.

questions.stem: A host moved ports but the recorded switch port remains old. Which observation is decisive?
options: Compare current FDB with the last successful L2 poll
Only the RADIUS server's certificate expiration date
Only the host's DNS resolver search suffix
Only the switch's global STP root priority
feedback: The live forwarding table and poll timestamp reveal location staleness.
RADIUS certificate validity does not prove host-port mapping freshness.
DNS suffixes do not identify physical switch attachment.
STP root priority does not show a specific MAC's port.

questions.stem: Contact polling works, but L2 table retrieval fails. What should be validated?
options: Check plugin credentials and switch-output parsing
The guest sponsor's account expiration timestamp
The endpoint's browser safe-search preference
The FortiGate's IPsec phase-two selectors
feedback: Polling can fail at authentication or output parsing after contact succeeds.
Guest sponsorship does not read a switch forwarding table.
Browser preferences cannot affect switch management output.
IPsec selectors are unrelated unless the management path itself uses that tunnel.

questions.stem: A trap-triggered poll succeeded at 10:15 with a 15-minute interval. What is the next scheduled time?
options: 10:30, from the last successful poll at 10:15
At 10:16, regardless of the device's interval
At midnight, when all network devices poll together
Only after a RADIUS accounting stop arrives
feedback: Per-device scheduling uses the last successful read plus its interval.
Polling is not universally scheduled one minute after every trap.
Device polls are not necessarily synchronized to midnight.
RADIUS accounting is a different evidence channel.

questions.stem: A passive HA node is pingable but ignores RADIUS. Which boundary explains this?
options: RADIUS runs only on the HA node currently in control
The passive node lacks an Ethernet MAC address
Every RADIUS packet requires a shared GUI VIP
The switch must disable all server retries first
feedback: The HA role governs service ownership independently of reachability.
A reachable passive node has networking but may lack service listeners.
A GUI VIP is not a universal RADIUS service requirement.
Retry configuration affects failover experience, not listener ownership.

questions.stem: allowaccess lists RADIUS on the passive interface. Why may requests still time out?
options: The ACL permits traffic but does not start a daemon
allowaccess automatically forces the passive node active
RADIUS requires the node's web UI to be disabled
The secondary always shares the primary's process ID
feedback: allowaccess is a host ACL; HA control determines whether the service listens.
ACL changes cannot transfer HA control ownership.
Web UI availability is not a prerequisite for RADIUS listening.
Passive and active processes are not a shared PID namespace.

questions.stem: After recovery, the former primary stays passive. What does the HA guide require?
options: Manually restore primary control after recovery
Automatic primary takeover after every heartbeat
A forced factory reset on the current active node
Changing every endpoint's MAC address first
feedback: The guide says the primary does not automatically resume control.
Heartbeat restoration alone does not mandate preemption.
A factory reset is unnecessary and destructive.
Endpoint MAC changes are unrelated to HA ownership.

questions.stem: Which verification proves successful HA service takeover most directly?
options: Complete a RADIUS authentication through the new active
Both appliances answer ping on their management addresses
The passive node shows a valid license in the GUI
The HA link interface reports physical carrier
feedback: End-to-end authentication proves the new owner is serving.
Ping tests network reachability but not RADIUS service.
Licensing is necessary context but not a live transaction.
Carrier alone does not prove process readiness.

questions.stem: GUI access disappears immediately after changing the HTTPS certificate. What is the primary fault domain?
options: HTTPS certificate binding and Apache service startup
RADIUS accounting session record expiration
FortiNAC dynamic VLAN assignment policy
Wireless AP controller discovery and authorization
feedback: The selected GUI certificate can prevent the HTTPS service from starting.
Accounting data is unrelated to Apache management TLS startup.
NAC policy controls endpoints, not FortiAuthenticator web listener.
AP controller admission is a different control plane.

questions.stem: An HTTPS certificate warning appears but the login page loads. What is proven?
options: HTTPS answered but browser trust remains unresolved
The server certificate is trusted by every client
The RADIUS EAP certificate must be valid
The FortiAuthenticator HA pair is synchronized
feedback: A rendered page proves HTTP service and some TLS negotiation succeeded.
A warning explicitly indicates unresolved client trust.
HTTPS and RADIUS EAP may use different certificates.
GUI availability alone does not prove HA replication.

questions.stem: Which documented recovery is specific to an unusable HTTPS certificate case?
options: execute regen-cert force followed by controlled reboot
diagnose ips anomaly list followed by policy edit
set fgfm-allow-vm enable followed by device add
set storm-control-mode override followed by port bounce
feedback: The Fortinet Community article documents regeneration and reboot for this issue.
IPS anomaly diagnostics apply to FortiGate DoS policies.
FGFM VM admission is a FortiManager control.
Storm control changes switch ingress behavior.

questions.stem: Before replacing the GUI certificate, which checks prevent avoidable lockout?
options: Check SAN, key, chain, backup, and console access
Only the RADIUS NAS-IP and shared secret
Only the wireless SSID channel and band
Only the FortiSIEM CMDB polling interval
feedback: Server identity, key availability and recovery access are essential.
RADIUS client parameters do not validate HTTPS server identity.
Radio settings are unrelated to the GUI certificate.
CMDB monitoring does not determine web-server TLS startup.

questions.stem: A target account cannot change its own password. Which changer identity is appropriate?
options: Use a privileged associated secret to change password
The same account in Self mode without privileges
An unauthenticated browser session on the target
The FortiPAM dashboard viewer's account
feedback: Associated Secret lets a separate privileged credential perform changes.
Self mode cannot bypass target account permissions.
An unauthenticated browser is not a supported privileged changer identity.
Viewing rights do not confer target password-change authority.

questions.stem: A scheduled rotation reports success but the next launcher fails. Which test is strongest?
options: Authenticate to target using newly stored credential
Check only that the scheduler fired on time
Confirm the secret folder has a friendly name
Check only the administrator's GUI idle timeout
feedback: A target login verifies vault-to-target agreement after rotation.
Job execution alone does not prove target acceptance.
Folder naming is unrelated to credential synchronization.
GUI idle timeout does not test the rotated password.

questions.stem: An SSH password changer hangs on one host after login. Most relevant suspect?
options: SSH prompt/expect or newline parsing mismatch
The FortiSASE DNS category block action
The FortiGate SD-WAN probe server selection
The FortiSwitch storm-control broadcast threshold
feedback: SSH changers depend on command/response matching and newline behavior.
DNS policy is a different traffic-security mechanism.
SD-WAN probes do not interpret remote shell prompts.
Switch broadcast metering does not parse SSH command output.

questions.stem: Change Password Using is Self, Verify Password Using is Associated Secret. What follows?
options: Different identities may change and verify the password
Both operations must use the same identity
Verification is disabled whenever change uses Self
The associated secret automatically becomes a user approver
feedback: FortiPAM separately selects identities for changing and verifying.
The two identity selectors are independent.
A verifier can still run when Self performs the change.
Password verification and approval workflows are distinct.

questions.stem: Two appliances sharing a VIP merge into one CMDB record. Which documented corrective concept applies?
options: Mark the VIP in discovery settings and rediscover
Increase syslog severity to debug on both devices
Disable every parser that receives device events
Move all devices into the same organization
feedback: The discovery VIP list prevents a shared address from implying identity.
Syslog verbosity does not fix CMDB identity merging.
Parsers act on events, not discovery identity resolution.
Organization collapse can create additional tenancy errors.

questions.stem: A device appears in CMDB but its Monitor Status is Critical. What should be examined?
options: Monitor Performance errors and last poll timestamps
Only the successful initial discovery timestamp
Only the dashboard widget's color selection
Only the source's firewall-policy UUID
feedback: Monitor Status reflects ongoing job health and lag.
Discovery success does not prove later monitoring.
Widget styling is unrelated to polling.
Firewall UUID alone does not identify collector scheduling.

questions.stem: Discovery exceeds device licensing and some records become Unmanaged. What does that imply?
options: Those devices are not monitored as managed sources
All excess devices continue full metric collection
Every device is automatically assigned more licenses
Only the dashboard display is affected by the limit
feedback: Fortinet documents that Unmanaged devices are not monitored or logged as managed.
Unmanaged state is a functional capacity boundary.
Discovery does not automatically expand entitlement.
Licensing affects monitoring, not just presentation.

questions.stem: A one-minute poll runs every three minutes on a remote Collector. What design change best addresses lag?
options: Rebalance collectors or tune polling intervals and rules
Increase the event parser's regular-expression complexity
Change all CMDB object names to shorter strings
Disable the target's NTP time synchronization
feedback: Collector load and WAN latency can cause polling lag; interval changes affect rules.
Parser complexity does not repair a metric scheduling backlog.
Names are not the primary cause of delayed polling.
NTP removal worsens temporal evidence and does not improve collection.

questions.stem: A DNS category rating service is unreachable and the profile allows rating errors. What can happen?
options: Requests proceed with a logged rating-error condition
All DNS responses are forcibly redirected to the block portal
FortiSASE silently disables every firewall policy
The endpoint automatically switches to a private IPsec tunnel
feedback: Allow-on-rating-error is an explicit fail-open DNS behavior.
Redirect is a configured category action, not mandatory on rating errors.
A rating error does not remove unrelated firewall policies.
DNS rating failure does not create a VPN.

questions.stem: Safe-search enforcement fails while DNS category blocking works. What should be checked?
options: Deep-inspection policy and certificate-only override
The FortiSwitch unknown-unicast storm threshold
The FortiPAM associated secret's password age
The FortiNAC L2 polling device group interval
feedback: Fortinet notes safe-search enforcement needs deep inspection.
Switch L2 meters do not enforce web search restrictions.
PAM credential rotation does not control DNS safe search.
NAC polling does not define SASE TLS inspection.

questions.stem: A DNS request is allowed, but a later HTTPS connection is blocked. Which explanation fits?
options: DNS permits resolution; later application policy can block
DNS allow automatically exempts the full HTTP URL
The DNS filter rewrites all destination firewall rules
FortiGuard category decisions apply only to IPv6
feedback: DNS filtering permits name resolution without guaranteeing later application access.
DNS allow is not a full-path web-policy exemption.
DNS verdicts do not rewrite the firewall rule base.
DNS filtering is not inherently IPv6-only.

questions.stem: A DNS response succeeds during a FortiGuard rating outage. What conclusion is unsafe?
options: FortiGuard explicitly rated the domain as safe
The endpoint received some DNS answer
The configured profile may permit rating errors
The DNS request reached a resolver path
feedback: Fail-open can allow unresolved ratings; success does not prove safe classification.
A successful response does indicate some answer was returned.
The profile may indeed allow rating errors.
A response implies a DNS resolution path existed.

questions.stem: After factory reset on a supported 7.6.5 dual-WAN model, which default objects are expected?
options: wan1/wan2 DHCP, sd-wan zone and Default_Ping
Two static WAN IPs and a mandatory MPLS tunnel
A prebuilt BGP overlay with two route reflectors
An automatic packet-duplication service rule
feedback: The documented baseline creates DHCP WAN members, zone and SLA.
Static addressing and MPLS are not the default baseline.
BGP overlays require explicit design and configuration.
Packet duplication is a separate SD-WAN capability.

questions.stem: The sd-wan zone exists and SLA probes pass, but users cannot browse. What is still required?
options: Matching policy, eligible route, and NAT are still needed
Only a successful ping to the FortiGate loopback
Only the presence of the zone object name
Only an enabled FortiAnalyzer report schedule
feedback: Zone/SLA success does not replace route and policy admission.
Loopback ping does not test LAN-to-WAN forwarding.
A zone object without policy/routing is insufficient.
Reporting schedules do not permit user sessions.

questions.stem: An upgraded production FortiGate lacks the factory-default dual-WAN objects. What is the right inference?
options: Factory defaults do not necessarily apply on upgrade
The SD-WAN subsystem is necessarily corrupted
All WAN interfaces must be switched to PPPoE
Every firewall policy must be deleted and recreated
feedback: The feature is a supported-model factory-default behavior, not universal upgrade migration.
Absence after upgrade is not proof of corruption.
PPPoE is not a requirement for default DHCP WANs.
Wholesale policy deletion is unjustified.

questions.stem: A FortiManager template replaces factory WAN objects after ZTP. What evidence identifies ownership?
options: Diff factory reset and FortiManager-installed settings
Look only at the default DNS probe IPs
Look only at FortiSwitch LLDP neighbor entries
Look only at the FortiAP wireless channel plan
feedback: A before/after config diff shows provisioning overwrites.
Probe addresses alone do not identify who modified objects.
LLDP neighbors do not prove SD-WAN configuration provenance.
Wireless radio channels are unrelated to WAN object ownership.

questions.stem: A DoS policy drops SYNs, yet the firewall-policy counter stays flat. What does this imply?
options: DoS may reject packets before forward-policy matching
The firewall policy has no enabled security profiles
The TCP server must have a bad TLS certificate
The route lookup must always be successful
feedback: DoS evaluation precedes forwarding policy; no hit is expected for blocked packets.
Profile status cannot explain the early drop by itself.
TLS certificates are irrelevant before the TCP handshake.
An early DoS drop may occur without completing route evaluation.

questions.stem: A correlation handler fires but the incident has the wrong subject. Which field deserves review?
options: Check the join fields shared between correlation rules
The PDF report's page margin configuration
The switch's port-level storm-control burst setting
The FortiGate WAN interface's DHCP lease timer
feedback: The cross-rule join fields determine which records share a subject.
Report formatting does not define event correlation subjects.
Switch traffic limits do not map log identities.
WAN DHCP timing is not a correlation-field mapping.
